notes: Помета — «(সুহই)», рага сухаи (ср. сноску 25). pdf 176 (печ. с. 171). Две половины в строке. «Подобного нигде не видано» — hena nā dekhi yene: yene — вероятно, «где-либо»; чтение неясно. «Истома» — alasa. «Без отдыха на ложе» — śayana bine. «Телу станет тяжелее» — pīṛā bāṛiba dehe, букв. «в теле усилится недомогание». «Нитая Тхакура» — nitāi ṭhākure: Нитьянанда жил в доме Шриваса (ЧБ, Мадхья 4). «Не в силах удержать жизни» — prāṇa dharite nāre: о тоске разлуки; переведено точно. «Злосчастную ночь» — pāpiyā rāti, букв. «грешную ночь». «Каким Он стал» — ye haila, букв. «что стало»: состояние Гауры, расставшегося со спутниками; понимание неуверенно. «Прелестный обычай» — lalita rīti. «В пору прадоши» — pradoṣa kāle: этой строфой кончается прадоша. Подпись: «Нарахари».

verses.text:
В ночную пору полный расы Гора, войдя в прекрасную опочивальню, —
какой сладостный обычай! — лишившись самообладания, устремил взор на путь, которым придёт Вишнуприя.
Та юная жемчужина среди женщин с радостью в сердце, сидя в уединении, наряжается.
Изящно она убирает волосы; как [прекрасна] луна её лица, умащённая кункумой!
Синдур на лбу, узоры сандалом и прочим; как красиво [сияет] точка мускуса на подбородке!
В украшениях из разных самоцветов — какая красота! Нет подобной в мире.
Надев синее сари, — какое растёт веселье! — она переполняется несравненной любовью.
Она идёт к Владыке, жизни Нарахари; её тело сверкает, словно молния.*
Рага дханаши
notes: Пометы — «অথ নিশা—» («теперь — ночь», ниша: восьмой период; в сноске 5 он назван «нактой») и «(কানড়া)», рага канада — ночная рага. Строфа начинается на pdf 176 (печ. с. 171) и кончается на pdf 177 (печ. с. 172) «॥৩৪॥». «Лишившись самообладания» — dhṛti gata. «Устремил взор на путь, которым придёт Вишнуприя» — biṣṇupriyā gati-pathe nayāna diyā. «Юная жемчужина среди женщин» — naba ramaṇī-maṇi: Вишнуприя. «Наряжается» — biracaye beśa. «Умащённая кункумой» — kuṅkumete māji. «Синдур» — sindūra, красная краска — знак замужней женщины. «Узоры сандалом и прочим» — citra candanādi. «Мускуса» — mṛgamada. «Синее сари» — в печати похоже на nīpa; вероятно, nīla, «синий»: чтение неясно (синие одежды в падах носит Радха). «Переполняется» — в печати похоже на unaṛaye (OCR — unaḍuye); вероятно, umaṛaye, «переполняется, разливается» (ср. umaṛi, сноска 26): чтение неясно. «Любовью» — lehā (= sneha). «К Владыке, жизни Нарахари» — narahari prāṇa pahũ. «Словно молния» — taṛita: золотистое тело Вишнуприи. Позиция гаудия-вайшнавов — см. сноску 3. Подпись: «Нарахари».

verses.text:
Вишнуприя [идёт] к Возлюбленному, дорогому, как жизнь;
в [её] походке — какое новое изящество! — им уничтожена гордость многих Мадан.
Подойдя, — как сладостно! —
прикрыв лицо покрывалом, она смотрит уголком глаз на Луну Надии.
Гора, глядя на Возлюбленную, дорогую, как жизнь,
выходит навстречу, медленно-медленно, бережно взяв [её] за руку, ласково ведёт [её].
Приведя [её] к прекрасному ложу из цветов,
Он говорит слова, полные расы; слыша [их], прекрасная от стыдливости ничего не отвечает.
Когда [Они] не мигая смотрят глаза в глаза,
она в упоении той расой тихо-тихо смеётся — сколько веселья в сердце!
Словно очень жадная пчела,
пьющая мёд лотоса [её] лица, Он опьянел, лишившись самообладания.
Тело наполнилось обильным трепетом восторга;
коснувшись пары золотых лотосов [её] груди, Он трепещет, словно молния.
Снова и снова обнимая [её], —
Нарахари отдаёт жизнь в дар Владыке; сердце волнуется от блаженства.*
Рага дханаши
notes: Помета — «(ধানশী)», рага дханаши. pdf 177 (печ. с. 172). Короткие и длинные строки поочерёдно — как в печати. «Им уничтожена гордость многих Мадан» — tāhe kata madana-garaba nāśe: Мадана (Камадева) — бог любви (ср. сноски 23, 26, 30). «Покрывалом» — ghughaṭe. «Ласково ведёт [её]» — ādari āne. «К ложу из цветов» — kusuma śeje. «Прекрасная» — dhanī: Вишнуприя. «Глаза в глаза» — в печати ā̃kho ā̃khi (= ā̃khe). «Жадная пчела» — lubadha bhramara. «Коснувшись пары золотых лотосов [её] груди, Он трепещет, словно молния» — kucayuga-hema-kamala paraśi kā̃paye bijuri janu: подлежащее не названо, понято как Гаура (продолжение стр. 11–13); «словно молния» может относиться и к Вишнуприи — понимание неуверенно. Строфа описывает ночные игры словами пад о ночных играх Радхи и Кришны; переведено точно, без смягчения. Позиция гаудия-вайшнавов — см. сноску 3. «Нарахари отдаёт жизнь в дар Владыке» — narahari pahũ parāṇa nichai: можно понять и «Владыка Нарахари…»; nichai — нирманчхана (ср. сноску 2). Подпись: «Нарахари».

verses.text:
Гора, самоцвет достоинств, — в скольких забавах! — играет с Вишнуприей.
Пришла усталость, тела увлажнились потом; Оба обмахивают Друг Друга краем одежды.
С истомой в телах, с ликованием в сердце, Оба в радости улеглись в любви.
Двое стали одним телом; несравненна в мире эта новая любовь.
Сияние тел Обоих прекрасно сверкает; непрестанно оно освещает покой.
Совершенно дивно — нет сравнения. Пусть Нарахари будет отдан в дар Обоим.*
Таковы восемь периодов [суток].
Рага вибхаша
notes: Помета — «(ধানশী)», рага дханаши. Строфа начинается на pdf 177 (печ. с. 172) и кончается на pdf 178 (печ. с. 173) «॥৩৬॥». Две половины в строке; язык — брадж-були. «Тела увлажнились потом» — ghāme titila gā'. «Обмахивают Друг Друга краем одежды» — duhu dõhe karu ā̃care bā' (bā' = bāo, «ветерок»). «С истомой в телах» — alasala tanu. «Улеглись» — śutala. «Двое стали одним телом» — duhũ jana bhela ekai dehā: переведено точно (оборот пад о Радхе и Кришне). «Новая любовь» — naba nehā. «Освещает покой» — ghara karaye ālo. «Пусть Нарахари будет отдан в дар Обоим» — narahari duhũ nichani rahu. Позиция гаудия-вайшнавов — см. сноску 3. Подпись: «Нарахари».

verses.text:
Какая дивная забава!
Кто [о ней] рассказывает [или] хоть раз слышит — может ли он от счастья удержать [себя в] теле? (Припев)
Сурадхуни, погружённая в достоинства Владыки жизни Вишнуприи,
рассказав многое подобным образом, считает свою жизнь благословенной.
Услышав из уст Сурадхуни те прекрасные деяния Луны Надии,
Ямуна, обессилев от упоения расой, не может от счастья сохранить самообладания.
Тихо-тихо она говорит Сурадхуни: «Эта Луна Надии —
жизнь любящих юных дев Враджи, силок для их сердец.
Всегда покорный их преме и расе, Он поглощён играми расы.
Кто другой узнает, что Он — тот самый, [что] этот похититель жизни нагари Надии?
Венец нагар играет в Надии, став сокрытым».
Ах, ах! Нарахари берёт на себя беды игр Владыки.*
Рага лалита-вибхаша
notes: Пометы — «ইত্যাষ্টকালঃ।» (так в печати; = ityaṣṭakālaḥ, «таковы восемь периодов») — конец рассказа Ганги об аштакалия-лиле, начатого пометой «অথাষ্টকালাঃ—» (сноска 5), — и «(বিভাষ)», рага вибхаша. pdf 178 (печ. с. 173). Стр. 1–2 — припев (dhru). Снова слова автора — рамка беседы Ганги и Ямуны (ср. 17.1–17.3). «Может ли он от счастья удержать [себя в] теле» — se ki sukhe dharite pāraye aṅga. «Сурадхуни» — Ганга (ср. сноску 3). «Владыки жизни Вишнуприи» — biṣṇupriyā-prāṇapati: Гауры. «Обессилев» — abaśa. «Луна Надии» — nadyāra cā̃da. «Любящих юных дев Враджи» — premabatī braja-yubatī-jana: гопи. «Силок для их сердец» — manera phānda. «Покорный их преме и расе» — tā'sabhāra prema rase baśa. «Кто другой узнает, что Он — тот самый, [что] этот похититель жизни нагари Надии» — āne ki jāniba sei ei nadyā-nāgarī-parāṇa-corā: Кришна Враджи и Гаура Надии — одно; переведено точно. Позиция гаудия-вайшнавов — см. сноску 3. «Венец нагар» — nāgara-śekhara: Кришна. «Став сокрытым» — gupata haiyā: Кришна, сокрытый в облике Гауры (ср. channaḥ kalau, «сокрытый в Кали-югу», ШБ 7.9.38). Где кончается речь Ямуны (стр. 7–11), в печати не отмечено. «Ах, ах!» — āhā mari mari: восклицание восхищения (ср. сноску 20). «Берёт на себя беды игр Владыки» — pahũ līlāra bālāi laiyā: bālāi laoyā — «взять на себя беду [любимого]», выражение нежной любви (ср. nichani). Подпись: «Нарахари».

verses.text: Ямуна, опьянённая высшей премой, снова и снова говорит Джахнави:

verses_en.text:
At dawn, in His own incomparable courtyard, Gora, full of merriment, is at play.
On all sides are the hosts of His dear associates; seeing the Lord's face, they are absorbed in bliss.
The night has passed: looking [that way], smiling, floating in happiness, all the people of Nadiya,
leaving their own homes, go to the house of Sri Shachi with graceful gait — with what delight!
Memory of the body is far away, they are greatly stirred — who knows the ways of this anuraga?
Entering the house with many graceful movements, seeing that beauty, they lose their composure.
Together with them the Ganga and the Yamuna secretly float in the ocean of the nectar of Gora's beauty.
Narahari gives himself up for the love of the two; how much the two say to each other!*
The Yamuna says — raga bhairava
notes: Raga vibhasha is a morning raga. pdf 161 (printed p. 156). The author's words. "Full of merriment" — raṅgiyā. "Absorbed in bliss" — ānande bhorā. "The night has passed: looking [that way]" — pohāila niśi pāne heri: pāne heri, literally "looking towards" — towards what is not said (probably Shachi's house) — the understanding is uncertain. "The people of Nadiya" — nadyā-nibāsī (so printed). "Greatly stirred" — ati se cañcala. "The ways of this anuraga" — e anurāgera rīti. "Entering the house" — printed bhubane ("into the world"); the sense requires bhabane ("into the house"), probably a misprint. "Secretly" — gupate: the Ganga and the Yamuna are the goddesses of the sacred rivers, who come unseen to behold Gaura. "Gives himself up for the love of the two" — narahari duhũ lehera nichani: nichani is nirmanchhana (see note 5 of kirana 16), here "I offer myself". "The two" — the Ganga and the Yamuna. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
The Yamuna, in great joy of heart, tenderly taking the Suradhuni by the hand,
softly, softly speaks sweet words, showing [her] honour in every way:
"You are most experienced, you know rasa, you are blessed — who could find a comparison for you?
I long to hear [it] from your lips — oh, do not be the least bit hesitant in your heart:
regarding me as your own, tell me in private of the deeds of Gaurangachanda;
relating in order [His] pastimes with Vishnupriya by day and by night, dispel my longing."
Hearing [this], the Suradhuni, after expressing humility, modesty and so on, with great joy in her heart
lovingly tells the Yamuna the most charming pastimes of Narahari's Lord.*
The Ganga says — raga vibhasha
notes: The heading is "যমুনাহ—(ভৈরব)" ("the Yamuna says"). The stanza begins on pdf 161 (printed p. 156) and ends on pdf 162 (printed p. 157) with "॥২॥". Lines 1–2 and 7–8 are the author's words, lines 3–6 the Yamuna's speech. "The Suradhuni" — suradhanī / suradhuni, the Ganga. "Showing [her] honour in every way" — kata kata mate ādara kari. "Most experienced" — supravīṇā. "You know rasa" — rasikinī. "Blessed" — dhanī. "Do not be the least bit hesitant in your heart" — kichu nā saṅkoca kariha cite. "Regarding me as your own" — āpana jāniye. "Gaurangachanda" — gaurāṅga-cā̃da. "In order … by day and by night" — dibāniśi krama: in the order of the periods of the day (cf. 17.4). "Dispel my longing" — ghucāha byathā (printed like bethā). "Humility, modesty and so on" — dainya binayādi: the Ganga, as is fitting, first speaks of her own unworthiness. "The most charming pastimes of Narahari's Lord" — narahari pahũ līlā sulalita. Here a new kind of mood begins: the account of the ashtakaliya-lila of Gaura and Vishnupriya — Their pastimes by day and by night, beginning with nishanta (17.5–17.7) — in the words with which the padas describe the nishanta-lila of Radha and Krishna (rasa-lampaṭa, rasika nāgara, nāgara-rāya). Vishnupriya is Gaura's consort in Navadvipa, revered by the Gaudiya Vaishnavas (on the wedding of Gaura and Vishnupriya, CB Adi 15). Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, following the Chaitanya-bhagavata (Adi 15: in His lila the Lord did not jest with women and did not even look at them), rejected gaura-nagari-vada — the worship of Gaura as an enjoying lover (nāgara): Gaura is Krishna in the mood of Radha, tasting Her love, not the enjoyer. Cf. the main notes of kiranas 11 (note 2), 12 (note 10), 14 (note 2) and 16 (note 2). Further notes in this kirana refer to this one. Signature: "Narahari's Lord".

verses_en.text:
"Listen, listen, O playful Yamuna, to the lovely deeds of the Moon of Nadiya!
With His beauty and qualities He enchants the minds of all: in the three worlds no one keeps composure.
All the delights that are in Nadiya — not even Shesha, Shiva or Vidhi can describe them.
All the wishes He fulfils in secret He reveals to no one except those who know [His] heart.
Moment by moment He goes about in the fresh manner of a nagara — how can His attire and ornaments be described?
All the women of good families in Nadiya worship [Him] — and yet they cannot see [Him] near.
If one of them, on some pretext, sees [Him] even once, she gives Him her life and youth.
Narahari's Lord is the embodiment of love; for love's sake, what will one not do?"*
Now — the eight periods [of the day].
Raga bhairava
notes: The heading is "গঙ্গা প্রাহ—(বিভাষ)" ("the Ganga said"). pdf 162 (printed p. 157). "Playful" — raṅgiṇi. "The Moon of Nadiya" — nadīyā-cānda. "Shesha, Shiva or Vidhi" — śeṣa śiba bihi: Vidhi is Brahma (cf. 13.5). "All the wishes He fulfils in secret He reveals to no one except those who know [His] heart" — gupate sādhaye yata manoratha marami bine nā kahaye kāre: the subject is not named; it can also be understood: "all the wishes [the women of Nadiya] secretly cherish they reveal to no one except those who know the heart (marami)" — the understanding is uncertain. "In the fresh manner of a nagara" — naba nāgarāli chānde: nāgarāli — the ways of a nagara. "Worship [Him]" — ārādhaya. "And yet" — tamu (= tabu). "On some pretext" — kona chale. "She gives Him her life and youth" — jībana yaubana sõpaye tāre: translated exactly. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. "The embodiment of love" — pirīti murati. "For love's sake, what will one not do?" — pirite ke ki nā karite pāre. Signature: "Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahũ).

verses_en.text:
"O Yamuna, this Moon of Nadiya is the rasa of love, a treasury of rasa.
Who equals Sri Vishnupriya in qualities? Seeing her beauty, Rama is ashamed.
The secret heart of each is known only to the two of Them; neither lives without the Other.
All the pastimes of the Two by day and by night — who could tell them with one mouth?
Narahari is overjoyed at this. In order I shall tell something of the ways of [Their] pastimes."*
Of these, first — nishanta.
Raga bhairava
notes: The headings are "অথাষ্টকালাঃ—" ("now — the eight periods [of the day]") and "(ভৈরব)". pdf 162 (printed p. 157). The Ganga's speech continues (the address "O Yamuna"). Each printed line has two halves ("।" in the middle, "॥" at the end). The ashtakaliya-lila is the Lord's pastimes in the eight periods of the day: nishanta (the end of the night), pratah (morning), purvahna (forenoon), madhyahna (midday), aparahna (afternoon), sayahna (evening), pradosha (early night) and nakta (night). "The rasa of love, a treasury of rasa" — piritera rasa rasera rāśi. "Rama" — Lakshmi. "Secret heart" — marama. "Neither lives without the Other" — duhũ binā dõhe nā jiye prāṇe. "With one mouth" — eka mukhe. "The ways of [Their] pastimes" — bilāsa-rīti. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari" — merged with the Ganga's speech.

verses_en.text:
At the end of the night Gora, avid for rasa, the crown jewel of rasikas, full of rasa,
plays with Devi Vishnupriya on a charming new bed.
How [wondrous] in that rest — body blended with body — the beauty lights up the three worlds,
like a golden tree encircled by a golden creeper, like a garland of champaka entwined with lightning.
Knowing the time has come, a dear maidservant arrives and, smiling and smiling, puts her face to the little window.
Gazing and gazing at the sweetness of [Their] rest, her heart overflows with great joy.
To wake [Them] she utters lovely words, hearing which no one can keep composure.
Narahari's Lord, waking, opens His eyes a little — how steeped in drowsiness they are!*
Raga bhairava
notes: The headings are "তত্র প্রথমতো নিশান্তঃ—" ("of these, first — nishanta") and "(ভৈরব)". The stanza begins on pdf 162 (printed p. 157) and ends on pdf 163 (printed p. 158) with "॥৫॥". From this stanza the account (apparently still the Ganga's) is given in the third person, without addresses to the Yamuna. "Avid for rasa" — rasa-lampaṭa, literally "greedy for rasa": an epithet of Krishna in the padas. "The crown jewel of rasikas" — rasika-śiromaṇi. "Full of rasa" — rasera bhare. "Plays" — bilasaye. "How [wondrous] in that rest — body blended with body" — kibā se śayane tanu tanu miśā: translated exactly. "Lights up the three worlds" — trijagata karaye ālā. "Like a golden tree encircled by a golden creeper" — hema-taru hema-latā-beṛā; "a garland of champaka entwined with lightning" — taṛite jaṛita campaka-mālā: both bodies are golden. "A dear maidservant" — priya-dāsī. "Puts her face to the little window" — mukha gabākṣe diyā. "No one can keep composure" — dhairaja nā yāya rākhā. "How steeped in drowsiness" — kibā alasa-mākhā, literally "anointed with drowsiness". For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahũ).

verses_en.text:
The Moon of Nadiya, the rasika-nagara Gora, the jewel of virtues, at the end of the night,
giving up sleep, His heart thrilled with ecstasy, gazes at Vishnupriya's face.
With great care waking His moon-faced beloved, He takes her in His arms.
She, with drowsy eyes, seeing the face of her beloved, dear as life, smiles and floats in tears of bliss.
They speak words full of rasa to each other, arranging their attire in lovely fashion.
They place tambula in each other's mouths — what a sweet custom! — composure is not held.
Lip pressed to lip, slowly, playfully, They sink back again onto that bed.
Narahari again tries to wake [Them], yet even so They do not give up Their drowsiness.*
Now — the morning.
Raga lalita
notes: The heading is "(ভৈরব)". pdf 163 (printed p. 158). Nishanta continues. "Rasika-nagara" — rasika nāgara. "The jewel of virtues" — guṇamaṇi. "His heart thrilled with ecstasy" — hiyā pulakita. "His moon-faced beloved" — bidhu-badanī dhanī. "He takes her in His arms" — karaye kole, literally "takes on His lap / into His arms". "Dear as life" — prāṇa-priya. "Arranging their attire" — beśa biraciyā. "Tambula" — betel (cf. 14.6). "Composure is not held" — dhṛti nā bāndhe. "Lip pressed to lip, slowly, playfully, They sink back again onto that bed" — adhare adhara dhari dhīre puna aṅga gaṛāyaye raṅge se śeje: translated exactly. "Narahari again tries to wake [Them]" — narahari phiri jāgāite karu yatana: the poet puts himself in the place of the maidservant who wakes the Divine Couple (cf. 17.5, lines 5–7); it can also be understood: "the maidservant again tries to wake [Them]; [so says] Narahari". "Even so" — tamu (= tabu). For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3.

verses_en.text:
Gora, the jewel of virtues, waking at dawn, cannot hold His composure;
filling His eyes, He gazes at the face of the moon-faced one and wakes her in a sweet manner.
In the absorption of that rasa, speaking softly, softly, how tenderly He treats her!
Arranging His garment, smiling, the king of nagaras leaves the bed.
Knowing that His beloved's heart is troubled, embracing [her] again and again,
He goes out of the chamber slowly, slowly, carefully holding His composure.
Turning, He looks again from the corner of His eye — what sweet beauty!
The deeds of Narahari's Lord, the crown of rasikas, entice the world.*
Raga vibhasha
notes: The headings are "অথ প্রাতঃ—" ("now — the morning", pratah) and "(ললিত)". pdf 163 (printed p. 158). Raga lalita is a morning raga. "Cannot hold His composure" — nā dhairaja bāndhe. "The moon-faced one" — śaśimukhī: Vishnupriya. "In a sweet manner" — madhura chānde. "In the absorption of that rasa" — se rasa ābeśe. "How tenderly He treats her" — kata nā ādari tāya, literally "showing her so much affection". "Arranging His garment" — sambari basana. "The king of nagaras" — nāgara-rāya. "Troubled" — biyākula. "Embracing" — āliṅgana kari. "Out of the chamber" — mandira bāhire: mandira here means "chamber, house". "From the corner of His eye" — ā̃khi-koṇe. "The crown of rasikas" — rasika-śekhara. "Entice the world" — bhubana-lobhā. The stanza ends on pdf 163 with "॥৭॥"; pdf 164 begins with a new stanza, 17.8 ("বিভাষ", "প্রভাত সময় গোরা…") — the next portion. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari's Lord" (narahari-pahũ).

verses_en.text:
At the hour of dawn Gora, full of rasa, floating in rasa, comes and sits down [in His place];
there His dear servant, rejoicing, brings fragrant water, filling a pitcher, and offers [it].
Having bowed to His elders, having finished the morning rites, surrounded by His associates,
looking at Gadadhara's face, He laughs — with what delight! — telling of former pastimes.
Mukunda and Madhava, in sweet ragas, pour out in song the nectar of those deeds;
hearing [it], He tries to keep His composure — and yet there is no steadiness in His heart.
Seeing these movements, someone says with what merriment: "This Gora is like the nagara of Gokula!"
Someone says: "This Lord of Narahari is the thief of the lives of the nagaris of Nadiya!"*
Raga lalita
notes: The heading is "(বিভাষ)". pdf 164 (printed p. 159). The morning (pratah; cf. note 8) continues. "Full of rasa, floating in rasa" — rasamaya rase bhāsi. "Comes and sits down [in His place]; there…" — āsi baisaye yathā … yogāya tathā, literally "where He sits… there he offers". "His dear servant" — priya-dāsa. "Pitcher" — jhāri, a spouted water vessel. "His elders" — guru-jane. "The morning rites" — prātaḥ-kriyā. "Telling of former pastimes" — puruba bilāsa kaiyā (in print bilāsa resembles biśāsa; OCR bigāna): probably of the pastimes of Vraja; Gadadhara Pandita in Krishna's lila is Radha (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika). "Mukunda and Madhava" — kirtan singers (cf. 15.7). "And yet" — tamu (= tabu, as in 17.6). "The nagara of Gokula" — gokula-nāgara: Krishna. "The thief of the lives of the nagaris of Nadiya" — nadīyā-nāgarī-parāṇa-corā: translated exactly; these are the words of "someone" among those present. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "the Lord of Narahari" (narahari pahũ).

verses_en.text:
Gora at dawn, at play,
intoxicating the minds of the people of the three worlds, sports with His dear devotees.
Ah, what a way of prema!
Devi Vishnupriya, when closeness with the body of Him who is dear as life was broken off, became greatly distressed.
Quickly leaving the bedchamber,
having finished the morning rites, she speaks with her friends of Gora's qualities — with what fresh love!
At that time someone says softly:
"Sri Sita and Malini, together with Shachi, are coming to you, floating in tears of bliss."
Hearing [this], the lovely one quickly goes forward to meet them;
out of shyness covering the moon of her face with her garment, she bows — with what grace!
Sita, Malini, Shachi — with what happiness,
giving countless blessings, holding [her] to their hearts, with what tenderness they kiss [her] face!
All [of them], having allowed [her] to bathe,
go to see Gorachanda, [dear to them] as life; seeing [Him] — with what bliss the heart overflows!
Performing many auspicious rites,
all direct the servant Ghanashyama to fetch various things.*
Raga vibhasha
notes: The heading is "(ললিত)". The stanza begins on pdf 164 (printed p. 159) and ends on pdf 165 (printed p. 160) with "॥৯॥". Raga lalita is a morning raga. Short odd lines and long even lines, as in print. "At play" — raṅge. "Way of prema" — premera gati. "When closeness with the body of Him who is dear as life was broken off" — prāṇa-priya-aṅga saṅga-bhaṅge: after Gaura rose and left the chamber (17.7); translated exactly. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. "Bedchamber" — śayana-gehā. "With what fresh love" — kata ki naba lehā (lehā — "love"). "Sita" is Advaita's wife; "Malini" is Shrivasa's wife; both are Shachi's elder friends. "The lovely one" — dhanī: Vishnupriya. "Having allowed [her] to bathe" — snāne anumati diyā. "Gorachanda" — gorā-cānda. "Auspicious rites" — maṅgala rīti. "The servant Ghanashyama" — dāsa ghanaśyāma: Ghanashyama (Dasa) is another name of Narahari Chakravarti himself (see the notes of kirana 1); the poet places himself in the lila as a servant. This is the stanza's signature.

verses_en.text:
Devi Vishnupriya swims in an ocean of bliss, sitting in seclusion.
Fragrant oil and turmeric [she wished] to apply — with what care the maidservant rubbed [them on her]!
Bringing scented water and bathing [her], [the maid] dries [her] body with a fine towel;
dressing [her] in garments and ornaments, she beholds [her] beauty — as if streams of nectar were pouring down.
The lovely one with wagtail eyes, having finished her own tasks, carefully taking various things,
places them all in the room for the worship of the Deity; Shachi Devi, seeing this — what bliss she feels!
Together with Shrivasa's wife, in great merriment, quickly entering the kitchen,
with what skill she cooks! Narahari gives up his life for it.*
Raga todi
notes: The heading is "(বিভাষ)". pdf 165 (printed p. 160). "Fragrant oil and turmeric [she wished] to apply" — sugandhita taila haladi mākhiba(?): the reading is unclear — the last letter of the verb is indistinct (mākhiba, "I will apply", or mākhira; OCR mākhira); taken as Vishnupriya's words or intention. "Towel" — pānitolā. "As if streams of nectar were pouring down" — sudhā-rāśi bariṣe janu. "With wagtail eyes" — khañjana-locanī: lively, beautiful eyes. "Places them all in the room for the worship of the Deity" — debapūjā ghare dhare saba. "Shrivasa's wife" — śrībāsa-gṛhiṇī: Malini. "Narahari gives up his life for it" — narahari-prāṇa nichaye tāhe: nichaye — nirmanchhana, "offers himself up" (cf. note 2). Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Advaita's wife, Sita Devi, merrily entering the kitchen,
says to Malini: "Tell me, I will listen: what is Vishnupriya's cooking like?"
Malini says: "Listen, O lady! How much of all this shall I tell?
I have never heard with my ears, never seen with my eyes such an art of cooking!
She has cooked dishes — hundreds of kinds; how many shall I name? — no one knows [them].
Look here: it delights the eyes to see! I have understood: she is [Lakshmi herself].
The friends of this moon-faced one have prepared many kinds of fine offerings:
those of whom I have heard [that they were] in Nanda's house in the town of Vraja — they have appeared here."
Hearing this, Sita laughs softly, softly. At that very moment Ai came;
seeing the excellence of the cooking, she praises [it], looking tenderly at her daughter-in-law.
At that time someone very carefully says into the ears of Shachi and Sita:
"Give the Moon of Nadiya, Narahari's life, permission to bathe quickly."*
Raga amara-todi (?)
notes: The heading is "(তোড়ী)". pdf 165 (printed p. 160). "Advaita's wife" — adbaita-banitā. "Kitchen" — randhana-mandira. "O lady" — ṭhākurāṇi. "How many shall I name?" — kata niba nāma. "She is [Lakshmi herself]" — lakhimī eho. "Offerings" — upahāra: here probably the dishes they cooked. "Those of whom I have heard [that they were] in Nanda's house in the town of Vraja — they have appeared here" — brajapure nanda-mandire ye śuni tā̃hārā ethāi prakaṭa haila: Vishnupriya's friends are the same who served in Nanda's house in Vraja (by tradition Radha and Her friends cooked for Krishna in Yashoda's house); the understanding is uncertain. "Ai" — āi, "mother": Shachi. "Her daughter-in-law" — badhū: Vishnupriya. "The Moon of Nadiya, Narahari's life" — narahari-prāṇa nadiyā-cānde. Signature: "Narahari" (narahari-prāṇa).

verses_en.text:
Shachi Devi, filled with joy, speaks, looking at Gadadhara's face:
"This morning I saw that that body has grown thin; I understood from the signs that hunger torments [Him].
Child! Do not disregard [my] words: look, it is the time for bathing.
You know how to persuade Him; He will heed [your] words — I know.
Go quickly and tell [Him] to bathe; otherwise [my] heart is anxious."
Before Gora Gadadhara says: "Bathe together with everyone."
Nectar drips in that sweet speech; all are glad to bathe.
Softly, softly Narahari says: "It is proper to bathe at home."*
Raga todi
notes: The heading is "অমর(?) তোড়ী" (in print the second letter resembles g: "অগর"; OCR "অমর"; cf. "অমর পঞ্চম" before 17.15). A raga "amara-todi" is not known to us; possibly a misprint, or "অপর" (apara, "another [todi]" — after the todi of 17.11) — the reading is unclear. pdf 166 (printed p. 161). Each printed line has two halves ("।" in the middle, "॥" at the end). "Child" — bāchā: Shachi addresses Gadadhara affectionately. "That body has grown thin" — o tanu khīṇa. "I understood from the signs" — pāilu cina. "He will heed [your] words" — bāṇī mānibe. "Bathe together with everyone" — snāna karaha sakala sahe. "All are glad to bathe" — sabhe sināite ulāsa bāse. "It is proper to bathe at home" — gṛhe sināite ucita haya: probably rather than in the Ganga, so as not to delay the meal (cf. line 2). Narahari here is a participant in the lila, Gaura's servant. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Gora, the jewel of virtues, smiling sweetly, gave His permission, sitting in seclusion.
His dear servant, rejoicing, having anointed [Him] with fragrant oil, gazes at that moon of His face.
Knowing the time [had come], he bathed the Moon of Nadiya in a lovely manner.
How he dressed [Him] in fine garments! Seeing that beauty, who could keep composure?
Tying the ends of the thick locks, he throws [them] onto His back — like a stream of the Yamuna.
Drawing a tilaka of sandal on His forehead, he puts a necklace of jewels and pearls on His neck.
Taking Narahari by the hand, the Lord goes slowly, slowly to the room of the Deity.
Having worshipped, offering various things, from the fullness of bliss He cannot contain His heart.*
Raga turushka-todi
notes: The heading is "(তোড়ী)". pdf 166 (printed p. 161). Two halves per line; in lines 2, 4, 6, 8 there is no "।" between the halves. "In seclusion" — birale. "His dear servant" — priya dāsa. "Fine garments" — saruyā basana. "Tying the ends of the thick locks" — bāndhi agra-bhāga kuntala-bhārā. "Like a stream of the Yamuna" — the dark hair. "Taking Narahari by the hand, the Lord" — dhari pahũ naraharira kare: it may also be understood as "the Lord of Narahari, taking [the servant] by the hand" — the understanding is uncertain. "To the room of the Deity" — debera ghare: Gaura worships the household Deity. "Cannot contain His heart" — hiyā dharite nāraye. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
As Gora bathed,
so all bathed and came — to see [them] gladdens the soul.
Lord Nitai, in a lovely manner,
put on blue garments and ornaments — [seeing] this, who could keep composure?
That Advaita who attracts the world;
Gadadhara, Gauri[dasa], Gadadhara [Dasa] — and what is the beauty of Shrivasa!
Yadu, Mukunda and the others likewise:
they glitter in the middle of the courtyard, as if moons were rising.
Shachi, seeing this, in the fullness of bliss
tells Gadadhara, [dear to her] as life, to bring everyone to the dining room.
Gadadhara, in sweet speech,
conveys to all the loving words of Mother Sri Shachi.
Hearing this, all of them, laughing,
say so much to one another, with what gestures, floating in an ocean of happiness!
All go together with Gadai.
At that time the servant Narahari merrily washes everyone's feet.*
Raga amara-panchama
notes: The heading is "তুরস্ক তোড়ী" (the conjunct is indistinct: "তুরষ্ক"?) — raga turushka-todi ("Turkish todi"). The stanza begins on pdf 166 (printed p. 161) and ends on pdf 167 (printed p. 162) with "॥১৪॥". "Lord Nitai" — pahũ nitāi: Nityananda. "Blue garments" — nīla basana: Nityananda (Balarama) wears blue. "Who attracts the world" — bhubana-lobhā. "Gadadhara, Gauri[dasa], Gadadhara [Dasa]" — gadādhara gaurī dāsa gadādhara: probably Gadadhara Pandita, Gauridasa Pandita and Gadadhara Dasa (cf. 17.15, lines 5–6, where "Gauridasa" and "Gadadhara Dasa" are named); "Gadadhara, Gauridasa, Gadadhara" is also possible — the division is unclear. "Yadu" — yadu (?): the reading is unclear — the letters are indistinct (possibly baṛu); the person is not identified. "As if moons were rising" — cā̃dera udaya yena. "Gadadhara, [dear to her] as life" — prāṇa gadādhare. "The dining room" — bhojana-ghare. "Gadai" — Gadadhara. "Washes everyone's feet" — pāda pākhālaye. Signature: "the servant Narahari" (dāsa narahari).

verses_en.text:
At Sri Shachi's bidding, floating in happiness, all went into the dining room
and sit down in rows — seeing [this] incomparable beauty, whose heart would not rejoice?
Sita Devi carefully serves various sweets; all eat merrily.
What a sweet playful quarrel Advaita carries on with Nitaichanda!
Gadadhara, Shrinivasa, Gadadhara Dasa, Dhananjaya, Shridhara-vatu,
Murari, Mukunda, Sadashiva, Gauridasa, Vasu and others — masters of the meal.
Shachi Devi's heart overflows with bliss at the sight of the lovely sport of the meal.
With the corner of her eye she says to Vishnupriya: "Fill a plate and give it to Malini."
Vishnupriya, arranging various dishes, rice and so on, gives [them] into Malini's hands;
hiding behind Malini, unseen, she beholds the Lord of her life.
Malini serves rice and dishes; they eat all this, which surpasses nectar.
Having finished the meal, He performs achamana; Narahari brings and offers water.*
Raga todi
notes: The heading is "অমর পঞ্চম" (raga "amara-panchama"; cf. note 13 — possibly "অপর", "another"). pdf 167 (printed p. 162). "Playful quarrel" — rasa-kalaha: Advaita and Nityananda banter at the meal (cf. CC Madhya 3). "Shrinivasa" — śrīnibāsa: Shrivasa. "Gadadhara Dasa" — dāsa-gadādhara. "Dhananjaya" — Dhananjaya Pandita. "Shridhara-vatu" — śrīdhara baṭu: baṭu — "young brahmin, brahmachari"; whether the word refers to Shridhara or names a separate person is unclear. "Sadashiva" — Sadashiva Kaviraja (?). "Vasu" — bāsu: probably Vasu Ghosha (cf. 15.7). "Masters of the meal" — bhojana-paṭu, "skilled at eating" — said in jest. "Fill a plate" — sājāyā thāli. "Hiding behind Malini, unseen" — mālinīra āṛe hai alakhita. "The Lord of her life" — nija parāṇa-nātha: Gaura. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. "Achamana" — rinsing the mouth after eating. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Gora, the jewel of virtues, with all the assembly, talks merrily of the meal.
All sit on many-coloured seats; the servants offer tambula.
Having eaten their fill, no one can remain sitting [any longer].
All, going each to his own lodging, lie down for a while.
The Lord lay down on His bed — the weariness of the meal went away.
The servants fan [Him]; Narahari serves those feet.*
Raga bhupali
notes: The heading is "(তোড়ী)". The stanza begins on pdf 167 (printed p. 162) and ends on pdf 168 (printed p. 163) with "॥১৬॥". Two halves per line. "Talks merrily of the meal" — bhojana-kautuka kathā. "Many-coloured seats" — bicitra āsane. "Having eaten their fill" — paripūrṇa bhojana-prakāre. "His own lodging" — nija nija bāsā. "Lay down on His bed" — śeje aṅga gaṛāila. "Fan [Him]" — karaye bātāsa. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Shachi Devi says to Sita and Malini, [sitting] beside her, in speech sweet as nectar:
"Eat, taking all these with you; let my daughter-in-law serve — this is the wish of my heart."
Hearing [this], they reply with great joy and sat down to eat, taking Shachi with them.
Vishnupriya serves [them]; [her] heart overflows with the fullness of bliss.
Rice and many different dishes they eat, praising [them], with what merriment!
Seeing that the meal is finished, the maidservants bring and offer water.
Having rinsed her mouth, Malini quickly comes and, smiling, says to Vishnupriya:
"You eat with your own friends; now I shall serve."
Having said this, unable to restrain herself for affection, she seats [them] beautifully in a circle.
Seeing that beauty — what thrills of ecstasy in her body! — Devi Malini merrily serves [them].
The lovely one, taking the nectar of her Beloved's lips, eats, giving [it] to many of her friends.
Having finished the meal — what happiness in her heart! — she washes her face with cool water.
Going into seclusion, she takes tambula; Shachi and Sita, seeing [this], are gladdened at heart.
What will Narahari understand of this way? The morning pastimes are most charming.*
Now — the forenoon period.
Raga deshapala
notes: The heading is "(ভূপালী)", raga bhupali. pdf 168 (printed p. 163). Two halves per line. "Daughter-in-law" — badhū: Vishnupriya. "Taking Shachi with them" — śacīre laiyā. "Having rinsed her mouth" — ācāiyā. "Unable to restrain herself for affection" — snehe thira nā bāndhe. "In a circle" — maṇḍali chānde. "The nectar of her Beloved's lips" — priya-adharāmṛta: the remnants of Gaura's meal, sanctified by His lips (adharāmṛta); Vishnupriya shares them with her friends. "What will Narahari understand of this way?" — ki bujhiba narahari e rīti. "The morning pastimes" — prātaḥkāla līlā: with this stanza the pratah period ends. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
The wondrous Gora in the forenoon, leaving His bed, sits alone in seclusion;
with cool water He washes the drowsy lotuses of His eyes and the moon of His face.
With a lovely movement He looks all around; Vishnupriya, unseen, seeing this,
covering her face with her garment, laughs softly, softly; out of shyness she cannot meet [His] eyes.
When the Lord full of rasa grew restless, His glance fell on Vishnupriya;
He cannot hold [them] back: the birds of His eyes, flying up and alighting, drink the sweet nectar of [her] face.
The bodies of the Two thrill ceaselessly with ecstasy; eyes upon eyes — what play, what a manner!
May Narahari be offered up to this sport! Seeing it, some are intoxicated with merriment.*
Raga mayura
notes: The headings are "অথ পূর্বাহ্ণঃ—" ("now — the forenoon period", purvahna; cf. note 5) and "(দেশপাল)", raga deshapala (cf. 12.10). The stanza begins on pdf 168 (printed p. 163) and ends on pdf 169 (printed p. 164) with "॥১৮॥". "The drowsy lotuses of His eyes" — alasala ā̃khi-kamala. "Unseen" — alakhita. "She cannot meet [His] eyes" — dite nāre ā̃khete ā̃khi. "The Lord full of rasa grew restless" — rasamaya pahũ byākula haite. "The birds of His eyes, flying up and alighting, drink the sweet nectar of [her] face" — ā̃khi-pākhī uṛi paṛi piye mukha amiyā miṭhi: the figure of the chakora drinking moonlight. "Eyes upon eyes — what play, what a manner" — nayāne nayāne bhaṅgi ki bhāti. Translated exactly. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. "May Narahari be offered up to this sport" — narahari rahu nichani e raṅga: nichani — nirmanchhana (cf. note 2). "Some" — keho keho: probably the maidservants. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Ah, what a sweet manner!
The Two, looking at each other eye to eye — the heart keeps no composure.
Vishnupriya, filled with that rasa,
quickly preparing tambula, joyfully placed [it] in a maidservant's hand.
The maidservant, coming, smiling and smiling, says:
"Your Beloved, dear as life, has sent tambula; do as is fitting."
The Moon of Nadiya, opening that little box,
at the touch of the tambula rejoices in body, covered with thrills of ecstasy.
Having eaten the tambula with what delight,
He handed the maidservant the box with the remainder — saying so many things [to her]!
The maidservant, coming to Vishnupriya,
opens that box and, telling of many things, smiles sweetly, sweetly.
When Vishnupriya with delight
puts that tambula in her mouth — how much bliss wells up! — a thrill spreads through [her] body.
What little remained of it at the end —
that, the rarest of things, smiling softly, softly, she gave to the servant Narahari.*
Raga dhanashi
notes: The heading is "(মায়ূর)", raga mayura. The stanza begins on pdf 169 (printed p. 164) after the end of 17.18 (lines 1–4 of pdf 169 are translated in the previous portion). The forenoon (purvahna; cf. note 19) continues. Short and long lines alternate, as in print. "Ah" — āhā mari. "Manner" — chānde. "Looking at each other eye to eye" — in print harāhari duhũ ākhye ākhi diyā; harāhari is probably herāheri ("looking at each other"), ākhye = ā̃khe: the reading is unclear. "The Two" — Gaura and Vishnupriya (continuing 17.18). "Tambula" — betel (cf. 17.6). "Your Beloved, dear as life" — tuyā prāṇa-priyā. "Do as is fitting" — karo ye ucita haya. "The Moon of Nadiya" — in print it resembles natmābidhu / nagyāsidhu (OCR); probably nadyā-bidhu (cf. nadyā-nibāsī, 17.1): the reading is unclear. "Little box" — sampuṭa, a betel casket. "Rejoices in body, covered with thrills of ecstasy" — ulasita tanu jhā̃pila pulakābali. "With the remainder" — abaśeṣa saha: the rest of the tambula, sanctified by Gaura's lips (cf. adharāmṛta, note 18). "Saying so many things" — kata nā kaiyā. "The rarest of things" — se ati dulaha: dulaha = durlabha, "hard to obtain". "Gave to the servant Narahari" — dila narahari dāse: the poet is a participant in the lila, a servant (cf. 17.13–17.15). For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "the servant Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Vishnupriya with a friend merrily tells of the deeds of Gora.
[Her] body is pervaded with the fullness of thrills; without Gora she keeps no composure.
What the Lord will eat at midday — that she prepares with how much care!
Going to a most secluded place, she sits, putting her eyes to a lovely little window:
the Lord will come to the flower garden — how great the eagerness to see it!
What will Narahari understand of this way? Ah, a love unequalled in the world!*
Raga kamoda
notes: The heading is "(ধানশী)", raga dhanashi. The stanza begins on pdf 169 (printed p. 164) and ends on pdf 170 (printed p. 165) with "॥২০॥". Each printed line has two halves. "With a friend" — sakhīra saṅge. "The fullness of thrills" — pulaka bhare. "What the Lord will eat at midday" — pahũ madhyāhne bhuñjiba yāhā. "A most secluded place" — atibirale. "Putting her eyes to a lovely little window" — cāru gabākṣe nayāna diyā (cf. 17.5). "Flower garden" — puṣpa kānana: probably the garden by the house (cf. 17.25, "the garden near the house"). "How great the eagerness" — uchāha bahu. "Ah" — mari. "A love unequalled in the world" — jagate atula prīta. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Thinking of the deeds of Vishnupriya, charming Gora floats in an ocean of rasa.
Moment by moment, how much rises in [His] heart! Gora offers up His life to Vishnupriya's qualities.
Having become steady with how much effort, the Lord went and sat in the outer house.
There His dear associates gather. What will Narahari say of that happiness?*
Raga deshapala
notes: The heading is "(কামোদ)", raga kamoda. pdf 170 (printed p. 165). Two halves in each line. "Charming" — binodiyā. "Moment by moment" — tile tile. "Offers up His life to Vishnupriya's qualities" — nichaye parāṇa gorā biṣṇupriyā-guṇe: nichaye — nirmanchhana, "offers up" (cf. note 2). "Having become steady" — thira haiyā. "The outer house" — bāhira bhabane: the part of the house where guests are received. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Gaura is graceful, loving, full of rasa; [His] deeds are the great depth of the heart.
In meeting with all His associates, dear [to Him] as life, there is supreme joy.
Likewise the host of associates rejoices, seeing the face of the Lord of their life.
Speaking what sweet words, they sit in a radiant throng, surrounding [Him] on all sides!
In the midst of the lovely assembly shines the youth, the Subduer of Manmatha.
He sways with bhava, [on His body —] abundant thrills, His lotus eyes are filled with tears.
Taking Gadadhara by the hand, He reveals the excellent rasa of Vraja.
What will the servant Narahari tell of the pastimes of the forenoon?*
Now — midday.
Raga shri
notes: The heading is "(দেশপাল)", raga deshapala (cf. note 19). pdf 170 (printed p. 165). The language of the stanza is Brajabuli. "Graceful, loving" — sughara sanehi (sughaṛa, "graceful, skilful"; sanehī, "loving"). "[His] deeds are the great depth of the heart" — carita ati hiya thāha: thāha (Hindi thāh) means "bottom, depth"; possibly "[His] deeds [are grasped only in] the depth of the heart" or "the heart finds no bottom [to them]" — the understanding is uncertain. "Supreme joy" — parama uchāha. "The Lord of their life" — prāṇa-pahũ. "In a radiant throng" — in print chabipañje (OCR likewise); probably chabi-puñje, "in a throng of beauty": the reading is unclear. "The Subduer of Manmatha" — manoja-damana: Manmatha (Kamadeva) is the god of love; Gaura conquers him by His beauty (cf. 17.25, 17.29). "Youth" — kiśora. "Sways with bhava" — bhābe ṭalamala. "Lotus eyes" — jalaja-diṭhi. "Taking Gadadhara by the hand" — gahi gadādhara-kara: Gadadhara Pandita is Radha in Krishna's lila (Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika; cf. note 9). "Reveals the excellent rasa of Vraja" — bara-barajarasa-parakāśa. "The forenoon" — pūrbāhṇa samaya: with this stanza the purvahna ends. Signature: "the servant Narahari" (dāsa narahari).

verses_en.text:
The Moon Gaura, floating in rasa, comes and enters the flower garden at the midday hour.
The place is very cool; gently, gently a fragrant breeze blows pleasantly.
Sharis, shukas and flocks of cuckoos sing most charmingly of Gora's qualities, intoxicated with bliss.
Bees roam in swarms upon swarms and hum, as if instruments were sweetly playing.
Peacocks, spreading their tails, dance; seeing [them], no one can turn his eyes away.
Each displays its own qualities; who can describe the beauty of their varied plumage?
Blossoming trees encircled by rows of creepers — incomparable is the shade there, with what delight!
The Lord of Narahari, seated, smiles softly; abundant thrills gleam on [His] body.*
Raga suhai
notes: The headings are "অথ মধ্যাহ্নঃ—" ("now — midday", madhyahna; cf. note 5) and "(শ্রীরাগ)", raga shri. The stanza begins on pdf 170 (printed p. 165) and ends on pdf 171 (printed p. 166) with "॥২৩॥". "The Moon Gaura" — gauraśaśī. "Flower garden" — puṣpabāṭi. "Place" — thala (= sthala). "Sharis, shukas" — female and male parrots, the singing birds of the lila. "Flocks of cuckoos" — piku-kula (pika, the Indian cuckoo). "As if instruments were sweetly playing" — yena bāje yantra madhura bhā̃ti. "Peacocks, spreading their tails" — śikhi pākhī pākhā pasāri, literally "spreading their wings". "Varied plumage" — nānā pakṣa-śobhā. "Encircled by rows of creepers" — latāli-balita. "With what delight" — ki raṅge. Signature: "the Lord of Narahari" (narahari pahũ).

verses_en.text:
To Lord Gora it seemed as if He were sitting in a kunja of Vrindavana.
What a wondrous way of rasa! He looks in all directions, very restless.
Devi Vishnupriya, at the little window, with an unseen glance saw Him.
Who else will understand that new love? Without blinking she looks.
The Two, seeing each Other, keep no composure; intoxicated with that rasa, They smile softly, softly.
How much merriment grows moment by moment — how much of it can Narahari tell?*
Raga dhanashi
notes: The heading is "(সুহই)", raga suhai. pdf 171 (printed p. 166). Two halves in each line. "In a kunja of Vrindavana" — bṛndābana-kuñje: Gaura in the mood of Vraja. "Very restless" — cañcala ati. "At the little window" — gabākṣa-dbāre. "With an unseen glance saw Him" — alakhita diṭhe dekhila tāre: the subject is not named; understood as Vishnupriya (cf. 17.18, 17.20), but it can also be understood as "[He] with an unnoticed glance saw her"; cf. line 5 — the Two see each Other. "New love" — naba leha (leha = sneha). "Without blinking she looks" — animikha ā̃khe dekhaye seha: seha is "she" or "He" — the understanding is uncertain. Translated exactly. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Gaura, the youth of Vraja, the Lord who breaks the pride of Rati's husband,
plays in the garden of lovely flowers near the house, most sweet.
Some come, [others] go, beholding the Lord — an incomparable way!
At such a time Nitai and Advaita arrived there.
Sri Gadadhara and the other associates sit, surrounding [Him] on all sides.
No one's eyes blink — seeing the moon of Gaura's face.
As befits the hour, He begins to speak of former [pastimes] — a stream of nectar;
it overflowed and flowed in all directions. What will Narahari say of that joy?*
Raga saranga
notes: The heading is "(ধানশী)", raga dhanashi. pdf 171 (printed p. 166). The language is Brajabuli. "The youth of Vraja" — baraja-kiśora. "Who breaks the pride of Rati's husband" — rati-pati-garaba-bhañjana: Rati's husband is Kamadeva (cf. note 23). "Lord" — nāha (= nātha). "In the garden of lovely flowers near the house" — bhabana-samīpa sukusuma-kānana-māha. "Some come, [others] go" — kou āyata yāta. "Nitai and Advaita" — nitāi … adbaita. "No one's eyes blink" — kāhu nayana nā nimikha sañcaru: sañcaru — the reading is unclear (the letters are indistinct); understood as "no blink arises". "He begins to speak of former [pastimes]" — racai puruba prasaṅga: probably of the pastimes of Vraja (cf. note 9); the subject is not named — Gaura (or the assembly). "Overflowed" — umaṛi. "That joy" — uchāha. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Lord Gora with His associates plays in the flower garden with joy in His heart.
And here Shachi, the mother of the world, speaks most sweet words to her daughter-in-law:
"Prepare and give all the food: Nimai and Nitai will eat together with everyone.
Their bodies are tormented by hunger: They ate in the morning, and now it is already midday."
Hearing [this], the lovely one floated in joy and prepared everything before her mother-in-law.
Shachi Devi, calling Ishana, quickly sent off the various foods.
Advaita, with supreme bliss in his heart, seated everyone in rows to feed them.
In what a mood Nitai, the jewel of qualities, first put kshira and butter into Gorachanda's mouth!
Advaita cannot contain his heart: he puts kshira and cream into the mouth of Nitaichanda.
At the meal great merriment arises; moment by moment the waves of the ocean of happiness rise.
To behold the sport of the meal — how Brahma and the other gods long for it in their hearts!
What will the servant Narahari say? At the midday hour — most charming pastimes.*
Now — the afternoon period.
Raga bhatiyali
notes: The heading is "(সারঙ্গ)", raga saranga. pdf 172 (printed p. 167). Two halves in each line; after the first half of line 7 the print has "॥" instead of "।". "The mother of the world" — jagata-jananī. "Daughter-in-law" — badhū: Vishnupriya. "Prepare and give all the food" — deha saba sāmagrī sājāyā: sāmagrī — provisions, food. "Nimai and Nitai" — nimāi nitāi: Gaura and Nityananda. "Together with everyone" — sabhā laiyā. "Now it is already midday" — ebe haila duprahara, literally "now it is the second prahara". "The lovely one" — dhanī: Vishnupriya. "Mother-in-law" — śāśuṛī: Shachi. "Ishana" — īśāne: Ishana, Shachi's servant (cf. kirana 4). "Sent off" — to the garden where Gaura is with His associates (line 1). "Kshira" — kṣīra, thickened milk; "butter" — nanī, fresh butter; "cream" — sara, the skin of boiled milk. "Nitaichanda" — nitāi cā̃da. "How they long" — kata nā sādha. "At the midday hour — most charming pastimes" — madhyāhna kālete ati lalita bilāsa: with this stanza the madhyahna ends. Signature: "the servant Narahari" (narahari dāsa).

verses_en.text:
Who else will understand the secret heart of Gora? For half a moment He wanders alone in that garden.
The afternoon has come; floating in that rasa, He looks all around.
He sees Vishnupriya at the little window; with an unseen glance she saw Him.
Smiling softly, softly with the corner of her eyes — I do not know what she told Him.
That jewel among women, smiling softly, speaks with a friend — who knows of what?
The Moon of Nadiya with the rasikas again wanders through the garden together with everyone.
Seeing the beauty of the flowers — great delight! — He walks with slow gait to the bank of the Ganga.
What they say to one another, smiling — of that Narahari understands nothing.*
Raga paurabi
notes: The headings are "অথ অপরাহ্ণঃ—" ("now — the afternoon period", aparahna) and "(ভাটিয়ালী)", raga bhatiyali. pdf 172 (printed p. 167). Two halves in each line. "The secret heart of Gora" — gorā-marama. "Half a moment" — tila ādha. "He sees Vishnupriya at the little window; with an unseen glance she saw Him" — dekhe biṣṇupriyā gabākṣa-dbāre alakhita diṭhe dekhila tāre: the subjects are not named; it can also be understood as "Vishnupriya looks from the little window; with an unseen glance she saw Him" or "…He saw her unnoticed" (cf. note 25) — the understanding is uncertain. "With the corner of her eyes" — in print ā̃khora koṇe (= ā̃khira). "I do not know what she told Him" — nā jāniye kibā kahila tāne: the speaker is not named; probably Vishnupriya — with her glance. "Jewel among women" — ramaṇī-maṇi: Vishnupriya. "With the rasikas" — rasika saṅge: with His associates. "Slow gait" — manthara gati. "Understands nothing" — kichu nā bujhe. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Gora, the jewel of qualities, went slowly, slowly to the bank of the Suradhuni with happiness in His heart.
On all sides His dear associates shine — that beauty does not come to the lips to be told.
Hearing [of it] from one another, the people of Nadiya, keeping no composure, come running.
With what bliss their hearts surge as they look at the face of Gorachanda!
In the sky the celestial women with their companions, smiling at one another as if in play,
seeing that form which enchants the minds of the three worlds, float in the tears of their eyes.
The daughter of Jahnu surged up, joyful at heart in the hope of the touch of the Lord's feet.
What new, charming pastimes of the Lord of Narahari's life at the close of the day!*
Now — evening.
Raga gauri
notes: The heading is "(পৌরবী)", raga paurabi (paurabī; apparently a variety of raga purvi, an evening raga). pdf 173 (printed p. 168). "Suradhuni" — the Ganga (cf. note 3). "Does not come to the lips to be told" — kahite nā āise mukhe. "From one another" — āne āne. "The celestial women with their companions" — gaṇa saha suranārī. "As if in play" — kautuka-cchale, literally "on the pretext of play". "That form" — in print onā rūpa: onā is probably "that, His" (cf. Hindi un): the reading is unclear. "Which enchants the minds of the three worlds" — tribhubana mana-mohaniyā. "Float in the tears of their eyes" — bhāse ā̃khera jale. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3 (the celestial women, seeing Gaura's beauty, are filled with prema; cf. the main notes of kiranas 11–16). "The daughter of Jahnu" — jahnu-kanyā: the Ganga. "Surged up" — uthalala: rose in waves. "At the close of the day" — dibābasāne: with this stanza the aparahna ends. Signature: "Narahari" (narahari prāṇanāthera, "of the Lord of Narahari's life").

verses_en.text:
Gora, the crown of rasikas, merrily
plays at the evening hour with His lovely dear associates.
On the most beautiful bank of the Jahnavi
having stayed for some time, He touches the cool water and goes to His own home.
With what a graceful, slow gait
Hari takes away the pride of the elephant! [Even] Manmatha keeps no composure.
Coming near His own house,
glancing unseen on all sides, He saw the Beloved of His life.
He holds firm, [yet] composure cannot be kept:
His eyes — thirsty chakora birds — fly up and alight on the moon of [her] face.
What new love is Vishnupriya's!
Not seeing the Lord of her life for even half a moment, she cannot hold [herself in her] body.
Unseen, meeting [His] eyes with her eyes,
she thrills in body; in incomparable, dense bliss her heart surges.
Narahari does not grasp the secret:
the Lord, enchanter of the world, the jewel of qualities, enters the house.*
Raga gauri
notes: The headings are "অথ সায়াহ্নঃ—" ("now — evening", sayahna) and "(গৌরী)", raga gauri. The stanza begins on pdf 173 (printed p. 168) and ends on pdf 174 (printed p. 169) with "॥২৯॥" — translated in full. Short and long lines alternate. "The crown of rasikas" — rasika-śekhara. "Jahnavi" — the Ganga, "daughter of Jahnu". "Touches the cool water" — paraśi śītala nīre. "Hari takes away the pride of the elephant" — kuñjara-garaba hare hari: Gaura's gait is lovelier than an elephant's. "Manmatha keeps no composure" — manamatha nā dharaye dhṛti (cf. note 23). "Glancing unseen on all sides" — alakhita cāri pāśe nirakhite. "The Beloved of His life" — prāṇera piyā: Vishnupriya. "He holds firm, [yet] composure cannot be kept" — dhṛti dharu, nā dhairaja bā̃dhe. "Thirsty chakora birds" — tṛṣita cakora pākhī: the chakora drinks moonlight (cf. note 19). "She cannot hold [herself in her] body" — dharite nāraye dehā: she cannot bear [the separation]; translated exactly. "Unseen, meeting [His] eyes with her eyes" — alakhita ā̃khe ā̃khi diyā. "In incomparable, dense bliss" — anupama ghana ānande. "Does not grasp the secret" — nā marama bujhe. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari". The next stanza is 17.30 (pdf 174, "গৌরী", "গোরা রসময় মনের উলাসে সারিলেন সন্ধ্যাকালের ক্রিয়া…"), continuing the sayahna.

verses_en.text:
Gora, full of rasa, in the delight of His heart completed the evening rites.
The associates, absorbed in prema, went each to his own home.
Shri Shachi Devi, having carefully served Vishnu, joining her palms, speaks [these] words [to Him]:
"I pray to You: keep my Vishvambhara in well-being by Your own grace.
And I say more: my beautiful Nitai obeys no one — He is very restless.
What more shall I say? I am afraid at heart: rid [Him] of these boyish ways.
My daughter-in-law Vishnupriya — sweet is her nature; I hold her dearer than life.
May no misfortune ever befall her. To whom but You shall I make this known?"
Hearing His mother's words, Gora, the jewel of qualities, standing at a distance, laughs softly.
He joyfully bows at His mother's feet; Shachi Devi gives [Him] many blessings.
When her daughter-in-law bows, [Shachi], speaking honeyed words, embraces her again and again.
May Narahari be offered up! What a new loveliness of love at the evening hour!*
Now — pradosha.
Raga amra-panchama (?)
notes: The heading is "(গৌরী)", raga gauri (cf. 17.29). pdf 174 (printed p. 169); lines 1–4 of pdf 174 are the end of 17.29 (translated in the previous portion). The evening (sayahna; cf. note 30) continues. "The evening rites" — sandhyākālera kriyā. "Having carefully served Vishnu" — sebi biṣṇu yatane: the household Deity (cf. 17.13); Shachi's prayer is addressed to Him. "By Your own grace" — āpana guṇe, lit. "by Your own qualities". "Boyish ways" — bālaka rīti: Nityananda, like a child, obeys no one (cf. CB, Madhya 3–4). "No misfortune" — in print bibini; probably bighini (= bighna, "obstacle, misfortune"): the reading is unclear. "Standing at a distance" — dūre rahi. "Embraces" — karaye kole, "takes onto her lap, holds close". "May Narahari be offered up" — narahari rahu nichani (nirmanchhana; cf. note 2). "Loveliness of love" — prema paripāṭi. "At the evening hour" — sāyāhnakāle: this stanza ends the sayahna. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
At the hour of pradosha Gora, sitting in solitude — how sweetly! —
watches the road [by which] His dear associates [will come]; He cannot keep His composure.
At that time Gadadhara, Shrivasa and the others come with quick steps;
Advaita and Nitai — the Two have arrived; incomparable are the ways of the Two.
They sat down in rows, surrounding Gorachanda — with what happiness of heart!
Gazing at the incomparable beauty of the assembly, the eyes do not blink.
The former tales of Narahari's Lord they tell to one another —
as if a stream of nectar flows. Who can grasp such a play?*
Raga dhanashi
notes: The headings are "অথ প্রদোষঃ—" ("now — pradosha", the early night; cf. note 5) and the raga "আম্রপঞ্চম" (?): the reading is unclear — the second letter in print is a conjunct with ra-phala and looks like āmra-pañcama (OCR — āja-pañcama); possibly the same raga as "অমর পঞ্চম" before 17.15 (note 16). The stanza begins on pdf 174 (printed p. 169) and ends on pdf 175 (printed p. 170) with "॥৩১॥". "In solitude" — nirajane. "Watches the road [by which] His dear associates [will come]" — nirikhaye priya parikara-patha-pāne. "Incomparable are the ways of the Two" — atula dõhāra rīti. "The eyes do not blink" — nimikha nā bahe ā̃khe. "The former tales" — puruba kāhinī: probably of the pastimes of Vraja (cf. notes 9, 26). "Of Narahari's Lord" — narahari pahũ: the signature merged with the line; it may also be understood as "Lord Narahari tells…" — the understanding is uncertain. Signature: "Narahari's Lord".

verses_en.text:
Lord Gora sports in solitude; with His associates He floats in an ocean of happiness.
Shachi, hearing that all had come — what arose in her heart cannot be told.
Looking at the road, she says: "When will Sita Devi and Malini come?
In the afternoon they went home; the evening is passing — why have they still not come?"
At that time Sita Devi came; seeing [her] — what joy! — [Shachi] bows at [her] feet.
Seeing Malini coming, [Shachi] went forward and brought her, taking her by the hand.
When her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya bows to the Two, the Two embrace her with what tenderness!
Shachi Devi, in the delight of her heart, says softly, softly to her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya:
"The time for the meal has come." Hearing [this], Vishnupriya, smiling sweetly, says:
"All is ready — come and see." Hearing [this], all, with gladness of heart, go and see.
Sita Devi says again and again: "The time for the meal has come — why delay any longer?
Come to the meal with everyone." Hearing [this], Gadadhara goes and tells [it to] all.
All, in great delight of heart, entering the dining hall, sat down to the meal.
Sita Devi together with Malini serves [the dishes] with supreme bliss in her heart.
Having finished the merry meal and performed achamana, all go there [where they had sat] and sit down.
They partook of tambula, pleasing to the heart; how many merry plays arose — who can grasp [these] deeds?
Shachi Devi, very eager at heart, [wishes] to feed her friends Sita Devi and Malini.
The Two with their [companions], absorbed in prema, eat — what nectar! — Vishnupriya serves.
Having eaten and spoken many gentle words, Malini fed her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya.
The merry meal is charming: no one can leave Shachi's house to go home.
Sita Devi and Malini, as they gaze at Gora's face, have no composure in their hearts.
Taking leave of Shachi — as soon as they set off, Shachi's heart grew agitated.
What can Narahari say? All went to their homes with stricken hearts.*
Raga suhai
notes: The heading is "(ধানশী)", raga dhanashi. The stanza begins on pdf 175 (printed p. 170) and ends on pdf 176 (printed p. 171) with "॥৩২॥". Two halves in each line. "That all had come" — gamana sabhāra: the associates had come to Shachi's house (17.31). "Still" — tamu (= tabu, cf. note 9). "[Shachi] bows at [her] feet" — praṇame padatale: the subject is not named; probably Shachi bows to Sita, Advaita's wife; it may also be understood the other way round — the understanding is uncertain. "Went forward" — āgusāri. "Embrace" — kare kore. "Come and see" — in print dekhasiyā; probably dekha āsiyā: the reading is unclear. "Come to the meal with everyone" — bhojane āisaha sabhā laiyā: apparently addressed to Gaura; Gadadhara passes the invitation on to all (cf. 17.14). "Sita Devi together with Malini serves" — sītādebī mālinī sahite kari paribeśana: it may also be understood as "[Shachi] together with Sita Devi and Malini serves" — the understanding is uncertain (likewise line 21). "Achamana" — rinsing the mouth after eating (cf. note 16). "Pleasing to the heart" — manohita. "Her friends" — saiyere (saī, "friend"). "The Two with their [companions]" — dõhe gaṇa saha: Sita and Malini. "Malini fed her daughter-in-law Vishnupriya" — cf. 17.17. "With stricken hearts" — kātara parāṇe. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
What shall I say? Nothing like it is seen anywhere: Gora's happiness is the happiness in the hearts of all.
All the associates, in a lovely way, say softly, softly to the Moon of Nadiya:
"You have eaten — now drowsiness has come; without lying down the drowsiness will not pass.
If You do not lie down, discomfort will grow in the body. We will go and lie down in our own homes."
However many times they all said [this], they go, gazing at Gora's face.
Shrivasa, taking Nitai Thakura with him, went to his own home, agitated.
Advaita and the others go to their homes: without Gora they cannot hold on to life.
Some reproach the Creator: "Why did You make so wretched a night?"
Some say: "Make the sun rise — take away our sorrow right now!"
Speaking thus, absorbed in prema, they lie down and in their dreams see Gora.
Lord Gora, having sent everyone off — what became of Him! — seeing it, the heart breaks.
What will Narahari understand of this love? What a charming way at the hour of pradosha!*
Now — night.
Raga kanada
notes: The heading is "(সুহই)", raga suhai (cf. note 25). pdf 176 (printed p. 171). Two halves in each line. "Nothing like it is seen anywhere" — hena nā dekhi yene: yene probably means "anywhere"; the reading is unclear. "Drowsiness" — alasa. "Without lying down" — śayana bine. "Discomfort will grow in the body" — pīṛā bāṛiba dehe. "Nitai Thakura" — nitāi ṭhākure: Nityananda lived in Shrivasa's house (CB, Madhya 4). "They cannot hold on to life" — prāṇa dharite nāre: of the pain of separation; translated exactly. "So wretched a night" — pāpiyā rāti, lit. "sinful night". "What became of Him" — ye haila, lit. "what happened": Gaura's state on parting from His associates; the understanding is uncertain. "Charming way" — lalita rīti. "At the hour of pradosha" — pradoṣa kāle: this stanza ends the pradosha. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
At the hour of night Gora, full of rasa, entering the lovely bedchamber —
what a sweet way! — His composure gone, fixed His eyes on the path by which Vishnupriya would come.
That young jewel among women, with joy in her heart, sitting in seclusion, adorns herself.
Gracefully she binds her hair; how [lovely] is the moon of her face, anointed with kunkuma!
Sindur on her forehead, designs in sandal and the like; how beautifully a dot of musk [shines] on her chin!
In ornaments of various jewels — what beauty! There is none like it in the world.
Putting on a blue sari — what delight grows! — she overflows with incomparable love.
She goes to the Lord, the life of Narahari; her body flashes like lightning.*
Raga dhanashi
notes: The headings are "অথ নিশা—" ("now — night", nisha: the eighth period; in note 5 it is called "nakta") and "(কানড়া)", raga kanada, a night raga. The stanza begins on pdf 176 (printed p. 171) and ends on pdf 177 (printed p. 172) with "॥৩৪॥". "His composure gone" — dhṛti gata. "Fixed His eyes on the path by which Vishnupriya would come" — biṣṇupriyā gati-pathe nayāna diyā. "Young jewel among women" — naba ramaṇī-maṇi: Vishnupriya. "Adorns herself" — biracaye beśa. "Anointed with kunkuma" — kuṅkumete māji. "Sindur" — sindūra, red powder, the mark of a married woman. "Designs in sandal and the like" — citra candanādi. "Musk" — mṛgamada. "A blue sari" — in print it looks like nīpa; probably nīla, "blue": the reading is unclear (in the padas Radha wears blue). "Overflows" — in print it looks like unaṛaye (OCR — unaḍuye); probably umaṛaye, "overflows, surges" (cf. umaṛi, note 26): the reading is unclear. "Love" — lehā (= sneha). "To the Lord, the life of Narahari" — narahari prāṇa pahũ. "Like lightning" — taṛita: Vishnupriya's golden body. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Vishnupriya [goes] to her Beloved, dear as life;
in [her] gait — what new grace! — by it the pride of many Madanas is destroyed.
Coming near — how sweetly! —
covering her face with her veil, she watches the Moon of Nadiya from the corner of her eye.
Gora, looking at His Beloved, dear as life,
comes forward, slowly, slowly, carefully taking [her] hand, tenderly leads [her].
Bringing [her] to the lovely bed of flowers,
He speaks words full of rasa; hearing [them], the fair one says nothing out of shyness.
When [They] gaze unblinking, eye to eye,
she, absorbed in that rasa, laughs softly, softly — how much merriment in her heart!
Like a very greedy bee
drinking the honey of the lotus of [her] face, He became intoxicated, His composure lost.
His body filled with abundant thrills of ecstasy;
touching the pair of golden lotuses of [her] breasts, He trembles like lightning.
Embracing [her] again and again —
Narahari offers his life to the Lord; the heart surges with bliss.*
Raga dhanashi
notes: The heading is "(ধানশী)", raga dhanashi. pdf 177 (printed p. 172). Short and long lines alternate, as in print. "By it the pride of many Madanas is destroyed" — tāhe kata madana-garaba nāśe: Madana (Kamadeva) is the god of love (cf. notes 23, 26, 30). "Veil" — ghughaṭe. "Tenderly leads [her]" — ādari āne. "Bed of flowers" — kusuma śeje. "The fair one" — dhanī: Vishnupriya. "Eye to eye" — in print ā̃kho ā̃khi (= ā̃khe). "Greedy bee" — lubadha bhramara. "Touching the pair of golden lotuses of [her] breasts, He trembles like lightning" — kucayuga-hema-kamala paraśi kā̃paye bijuri janu: the subject is not named and is understood as Gaura (continuing lines 11–13); "like lightning" may also refer to Vishnupriya — the understanding is uncertain. The stanza describes the night pastimes in the words of the padas on the night pastimes of Radha and Krishna; translated exactly, without softening. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. "Narahari offers his life to the Lord" — narahari pahũ parāṇa nichai: it may also be understood as "Lord Narahari…"; nichai — nirmanchhana (cf. note 2). Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
Gora, the jewel of qualities — in how many plays! — sports with Vishnupriya.
Weariness came, Their bodies were moist with sweat; the Two fan each Other with the ends of Their cloth.
With languid bodies, with delight in Their hearts, the Two lay down in joy, in love.
The two became one body; incomparable in the world is this new love.
The radiance of the bodies of the Two flashes beautifully; ceaselessly it lights up the chamber.
Most wondrous — there is no comparison. May Narahari be offered up to the Two.*
Thus the eight periods [of the day].
Raga vibhasha
notes: The heading is "(ধানশী)", raga dhanashi. The stanza begins on pdf 177 (printed p. 172) and ends on pdf 178 (printed p. 173) with "॥৩৬॥". Two halves in each line; the language is Brajabuli. "Their bodies were moist with sweat" — ghāme titila gā'. "Fan each Other with the ends of Their cloth" — duhu dõhe karu ā̃care bā' (bā' = bāo, "breeze"). "With languid bodies" — alasala tanu. "Lay down" — śutala. "The two became one body" — duhũ jana bhela ekai dehā: translated exactly (a phrase from the padas on Radha and Krishna). "New love" — naba nehā. "Lights up the chamber" — ghara karaye ālo. "May Narahari be offered up to the Two" — narahari duhũ nichani rahu. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. Signature: "Narahari".

verses_en.text:
What a wondrous play!
Whoever tells [of it, or] hears [it] even once — can he, for happiness, keep hold of [himself in his] body? (Refrain)
The Suradhuni, immersed in the qualities of the Lord of Vishnupriya's life,
having told much in this way, considers her own life blessed.
Hearing from the lips of the Suradhuni those lovely deeds of the Moon of Nadiya,
the Yamuna, overpowered by absorption in rasa, cannot for happiness keep her composure.
Softly, softly she says to the Suradhuni: "This Moon of Nadiya —
the life of the loving young women of Vraja, the snare of their hearts.
Ever subject to their prema and rasa, He is absorbed in the plays of rasa.
Who else will know that He is that very One — this thief of the lives of the nagaris of Nadiya?
The crown of nagaras sports in Nadiya, having become hidden."
Ah, ah! Narahari takes upon himself the misfortunes of the Lord's pastimes.*
Raga lalita-vibhasha
notes: The headings are "ইত্যাষ্টকালঃ।" (so in print; = ityaṣṭakālaḥ, "thus the eight periods") — the end of the Ganga's account of the ashtakaliya-lila begun with the heading "অথাষ্টকালাঃ—" (note 5) — and "(বিভাষ)", raga vibhasha. pdf 178 (printed p. 173). Lines 1–2 are the refrain (dhru). These are again the author's words — the frame of the conversation of the Ganga and the Yamuna (cf. 17.1–17.3). "Can he, for happiness, keep hold of [himself in his] body" — se ki sukhe dharite pāraye aṅga. "The Suradhuni" — the Ganga (cf. note 3). "The Lord of Vishnupriya's life" — biṣṇupriyā-prāṇapati: Gaura. "Overpowered" — abaśa. "Moon of Nadiya" — nadyāra cā̃da. "The loving young women of Vraja" — premabatī braja-yubatī-jana: the gopis. "The snare of their hearts" — manera phānda. "Subject to their prema and rasa" — tā'sabhāra prema rase baśa. "Who else will know that He is that very One — this thief of the lives of the nagaris of Nadiya" — āne ki jāniba sei ei nadyā-nāgarī-parāṇa-corā: Krishna of Vraja and Gaura of Nadiya are one; translated exactly. For the position of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas see note 3. "The crown of nagaras" — nāgara-śekhara: Krishna. "Having become hidden" — gupata haiyā: Krishna hidden in the form of Gaura (cf. channaḥ kalau, "hidden in the Kali age", SB 7.9.38). Where the Yamuna's speech (lines 7–11) ends is not marked in print. "Ah, ah!" — āhā mari mari: an exclamation of wonder (cf. note 20). "Takes upon himself the misfortunes of the Lord's pastimes" — pahũ līlāra bālāi laiyā: bālāi laoyā, "to take the misfortune [of a beloved one] upon oneself", is an expression of tender love (cf. nichani). Signature: "Narahari".
